study type: Type I hybrid effectiveness-implementation study (before-and-after design)
cohort: The study included 8509 patients undergoing labor induction across two hospitals in the University of Pennsylvania Health System, with a median age of 31 years and diverse racial/ethnic backgrounds.
finding: Implementation of a standardized labor induction protocol significantly increased adherence to protocol components and decreased maternal morbidity, but showed no significant difference in the overall cesarean delivery rate or other neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the cesarean delivery rate after implementing the standardized labor induction protocol (PRE: 21.6% vs. POST: 21.8%, p = 0.85).
